problem: Dexterous visual real-worldRL needs task-directed exploration and stable low-level execution; offline demonstrations alone can be insufficient for difficult recovery states.
contribution: HIL-SERL combines demonstrations, online human corrections, balanced replay, taskreward classifiers and continuous/discrete control into a practical distributed learning system.
algorithm: RLPD actor-critic samples equally from a demonstration buffer andRLbuffer. Human correction transitions enter both buffers, while ordinary policy transitions enter only theRLbuffer. A separateDQN graspcritic selects discrete open/close/stay actions while the continuous actor controls end-effector motion.
observations: Multiple cropped128x128RGB views processed by anImageNet-pretrainedResNet10 plus proprioception and gripper state. Relative pose representations use the episode's initial frame; output motion is expressed in the current toolframe.
actions: Continuous end-effector actions plus discrete gripper actions. Contact tasks use impedance control/reference limiting; some dynamic tasks use feedforward wrenches. Neither capability follows automatically from a position-controlledSO101 driver.
embodiment_and_data: Physical single/dual-arm insertion, assembly, handover, Jenga andflipping tasks. Usually20-30initial demonstrations; a separate sparse reward classifier is fitted from positive andnegative examples. Source training uses a singleRTX4090.
experiments: Independent task evaluation compares success andcycle time, human interventions during learning, robustness perturbations and no-demo/no-intervention ablations. Running20episode training curves with interventions are not the final autonomousevaluation.
baselines: HG-DAgger with matched episodes/interventions, flatBC, DiffusionPolicy, IBRL, ResidualRL andDAPG; several baselines receive200demonstrations. Ablations remove demonstrations and/or corrections.

quantitative_result.source_inconsistency: Table1b listsDPdashboard18%, prose p17 says28%; that comparison is not silently reconciled.

limitations: Human setup, resets, reward data and interventions remain necessary; the current method trains each task separately. Source hardware/control affordances differ from low-cost servos. A high classifier accuracy does not itself establish physical task success or force safety.
hardware_adaptation: Reuse intervention/replay semantics and evaluate a compact compatible learner onNX. Keep Pi/Nano hardware authority local, and reject anywrench/impedance action contract the actual driver cannot implement. Begin with simulation/offline data; physicallearning needs explicit supervisionapproval.
algorithm_detail: Two replay stores distinguish trusted demonstrations/corrections from general interaction. Human takeover changes the action actually applied, so transitions must record it rather than the displaced policy proposal. A separate discretecritic avoids treating gripper categories as a continuousGaussian. Shared pretrainedvisual features reduce visuallearning cost.
integration_contract: Record policy proposal, takeoverflag, humancommand, dispatchedaction, observationcapturetime, rewardclassifierrevision and independently verified outcome. Maintain separate continuous-motion andgripper schemas. Pause cannot publish stale bufferedactions after ownershipchanges.
license_evidence: Officialrepository metadata identifiesApache-2.0 at the pinnedhead. Reading the paper andmetadata does not imply code inspection, installed dependencies orNX reproduction; those statuses remainfalse.
required_experiments: Replay routing assertions; matched-dataBC/HG-DAgger comparison; classifier calibration and independent successaudit; realNX optimizer/reload tests; correction/no-correction ablations; controlsupported-action admission andnetworkloss tests without physicalmotion.
difference_from_explorer: Already provides successful correction-driven physicallearning and a distributed architecture. Explorer must separately test cross-embodiment effectmemory, retention, composition and cause-selective repair rather than claim HIL-SERL's coreidea.
